title: Machine-learning phase picks constrain the 2025 Drake Passage earthquake depth and activated fault geometry
summary: For the Mw 7.4 Drake Passage earthquake of 2 May 2025, a trained classifier identified depth-sensitive pP–sP seismic phases used to refine focal depths under sparse station coverage. The authors infer a mainshock depth of about 25 km, consistent with the small tsunami, and report aftershocks on west-dipping faults southeast of the epicenter near the Shackleton Fracture Zone; the paper integrates this with seismic-reflection and previously collected imaging data.
ai_technology: Trained machine-learning classifier for depth-sensitive seismic phase identification
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS); CNR-ISMAR; University of Urbino; CONICET–University of Buenos Aires

evidence.tested: For the Mw 7.4 Drake Passage earthquake of 2 May 2025, a trained classifier identified depth-sensitive pP–sP seismic phases used to refine focal depths under sparse station coverage.
evidence.unknown: The result is a retrospective analysis of one earthquake sequence. The depth is inferred from phase picks and is consistent with tsunami observations; tectonic interpretation also relies on aftershock mechanisms and independent seismic imaging. The machine-learning component contributes phase identification rather than discovering the earthquake itself.
evidence.ai_role: Identified pP–sP phases in regional records; these phases were incorporated into event relocation and focal-depth determination, helping constrain the mainshock depth where station coverage is limited.
